title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
An Avride autonomous vehicle operating in Austin struck and killed a duck in a residential neighborhood while in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present. The vehicle did not slow down or stop for the animal. This is a failure of the perception and decision-making systems to recognize and respond appropriately to a small living obstacle in the roadway.

It is not established whether the vehicle's sensors detected the duck, whether the operator could have intervened, or what conditions would be required for the system to avoid similar incidents. The company stated the vehicle made appropriate stops at traffic signals and has since restricted testing on certain streets and begun controlled experiments, suggesting the incident revealed a gap between the system's design and real-world conditions it encounters.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An Avride autonomous vehicle operating in Austin, Texas struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood, causing significant community backlash. The incident occurred when the self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, ran over the duck without slowing down or stopping. Local residents had become attached to this particular duck, which was nesting near a nearby Italian restaurant, and some have rescued its eggs and placed them in an incubator.

Following the incident, Avride confirmed the vehicle was in autonomous mode at the time and reviewed the vehicle's data multiple times using simulation technology. The company denied a resident's claim that the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, stating it made complete and appropriate stops at all relevant intersections. As a response, Avride has restricted its testing operations by excluding certain streets around the lake and is conducting controlled experiments to improve the technology and prevent similar situations in the future.
